newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni journalist shot dead in more poll violence.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni journalist shot dead in more poll violence.

text.p: A Yemeni journalist was killed and four other people wounded in a shooting incident outside a vote-counting centre in fresh violence linked to Yemen's general elections, an official statement said on Thursday.
A security official said there was an exchange of fire between supporters of rival candidates but the official statement accused the Islamist Islah party of shooting at the centre on Wednesday.
"A journalist was killed when supporters of different candidates shot at each other after vote counting in Lahaj governorate," the security official said.

But the official statement said: "The killing was not caused by an exchange of fire...An extremist group belonging to Islah attacked the vote-counting centre and opened fire on those present, killing a journalist and wounding four others."
A Yemeni observer from the Arab Democratic Institute, a non-governmental organisation, was among the wounded, the security official said.
The dead journalist was named as Ali Mohammad Ajlan, but security officials declined to say who he worked for.
The killing raised to at least 21 the number of deaths related to Sunday's poll. Officials have played down the shootings as criminal and election observers noted that many Yemenis carry weapons.
The general election was the first since a 1994 civil war. The ruling General People's Congress (GPC) has swept more than 60 percent of constituencies in counting so far.
Islah, its junior coalition partner, lagged far behind with less than 20 percent. On Wednesday it accused election authorities of bias and threatened court action.
